as_told.title: Condon's Manhattan Project role and choice of Los Alamos
as_told.place_text: Los Alamos, New Mexico; Göttingen, Germany

plain: This story is about the physicist Edward Condon's ties to the Manhattan Project, the secret US effort in the 1940s to build the atomic bomb. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who says the government hides crashed craft not made by humans, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that Condon was involved, and he mentions Vannevar Bush, a top wartime science official. Michels fills in more. He says Condon is sometimes credited with helping Robert Oppenheimer, the bomb project's scientific leader, choose Los Alamos in New Mexico as its site. He says Condon was linked to the Los Alamos Primer, an early teaching document for the project, and helped with the McMahon Atomic Energy Act, the law that set up postwar control of nuclear matters. In a later episode Michels adds that Condon studied in Germany with the physicist Max Born and that he and Oppenheimer were very close. It is told because Condon later led an Air Force UFO study, and the link would tie that study to the world of nuclear secrecy.
